root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Tartakower Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 Be7 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bh4 O-O 7. e3 b6

overview: Black fianchettoes the queen's bishop and, after cxd5 Nxd5, trades pieces to free his position. White tries to use the c-file and a small space edge, usually with 8.cxd5 Nxd5 9.Bxe7 Qxe7 10.Nxd5 exd5 and Rc1, or 8.Bd3 Bb7 9.O-O. Black's position is sound and the play is strategic with real counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Trade on d5, then Rc1 and queenside pressure on a symmetrical structure
Develop Bd3, O-O and keep a small space edge

black_ideas.idea: Exchange pieces to ease the cramp, then break with ...c5
Bb7 and the fianchetto, hold the centre with ...d5 and ...Nbd7

typical_structures.structure: Exchange-style structure with a half-open c-file, or a fianchetto against d4/c4

character.notes: Piece trades and a stable position; Black is hard to break down and is rarely in danger early.

soundness.notes: Fully sound; a main-line QGD for decades.

structure.notes: Typically an exchange on d5 gives a half-open c-file; ...c5 break follows.

approach.notes: A standard theoretical branch of the QGD.

level.notes: Many sub-lines with specific move orders, but plans are clear.

character.reason: Black trades pieces and is hard to break down.

structure.reason: Exchange on d5 leaves a half-open c-file.

approach.reason: Played by top players as a standard QGD line.

level.reason: Specific move orders to know but clear plans.

plans.reason: White uses the c-file and Black fianchettoes on b7.
